extension.description: Analyzes the call hierarchy of a Java project in one pass and shows the caller tree and CSV for impact analysis
view.container.title: Impact
view.callers.name: Impact (Call Hierarchy Exporter)
view.welcome.contents:
Analyzes the call hierarchy of the whole Java project in one pass, so you can follow what a change affects.

The built-in "Call Hierarchy" (Shift+Alt+H) answers instantly from the open file; this one analyzes the whole project with Eclipse JDT first, then follows callers through interfaces and dataflow as well. The analysis takes a while.

[Analyze](command:jche.analyze)

Once it finishes, put the cursor on a method in the editor and choose "Impact: Show callers" from the context menu.
view.welcome.noFolder: Open a folder to use it.\n[Open Folder](command:vscode.openFolder)

configuration.jche.javaHome.description: Folder of the JDK used for the analysis (17 or newer; use 25 to match the CLI). Empty looks at `JAVA_HOME`, then `java` on PATH. The analysis runs in a process of its own, not inside VSCode
configuration.jche.libFolder.description: Folder holding the analysis engine (`jche-core.jar` and `jdt/*.jar`). Empty uses the `lib/` bundled with the extension. Set it to swap in a newer JDT on an isolated network, or to point at an `eclipse-plugin` build while developing
configuration.jche.vmArguments.descripti: Arguments passed to the JVM of the child process. Add things like `-Xmx4g` for large projects. Independent of the heap of VSCode itself.
configuration.jche.idleMinutes.descripti: Shut the child process down after this many minutes without a request (to give the memory back). `0` keeps it resident. The next request rebuilds it from the cache.
configuration.jche.configFile.descriptio: Config file used for the analysis (relative to the workspace folder). Empty uses `config.properties` in the folder root, and generates a config with only `project.root` if there is none
configuration.jche.depth.description: Initial depth one expansion of the tree goes to. Changing it in the view's filter settings remembers the new value per workspace. A node cut off at the depth limit fetches the rest when you expand it.
configuration.jche.autoAnalyze.descripti: Re-analyze in the background three seconds after a Java file is saved, added or deleted. OFF by default: it only counts the changed files and shows that in the status at the bottom right (the circular arrow re-analyzes).
configuration.jche.jdkDownload.descripti: Offer to download JDK 25 from Adoptium (Eclipse Temurin) when no JDK for the analysis is found (about 200MB; it always asks first). Turn it OFF on an isolated network.
